newsitem.title: USA: Astoria, Greater New York targeted by suit.
newsitem.headline: Astoria, Greater New York targeted by suit.

text.p: Greater New York Savings Bank, Astoria Financial Corp and Astoria Federal Savings and Loan Association were named as defendants in a suit seeking class-action status, lawyers for the plaintiffs said Tuesday.
The complaint seeks an injunction against Astoria Financial Corp's proposed acquisition of Greater New York Savings in a transaction valued at $293 million when it was announced March 31.

The complaint, filed July 18, alleges the companies and some of Greater New York's officers and directors issued a proxy statement that excluded some material facts, precluding shareholders from making an informed decision on whether to accept the proposed deal.
A spokesman for Astoria said the company would defend against the suit and did not expect it to delay the merger.
A spokesperson for Greater New York was not immediately available for comment.

The suit was filed in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York on behalf of owners of Greater New York's securities, a news release issued by New York lawyers Jack Zwick and Jules Brody said.

The complaint also alleges the officer and director defendants breached their fiduciary duties by agreeing to the offer, which contains special benefits to the individual officers and directors without properly safeguarding the interests of Greater New York's public shareholders, the news release said.
"Astoria believes the allegations made in the action are without merit," said Raymond Teed, spokesman for Astoria Federal Savings. "We are filing motions to have the suit dismissed."
Teed said a similar suit was filed in April in the New York Supreme Court and that suit is pending along with Astoria's motion to have it dismissed.
"We do not expect either the state or the federal suit to delay our merger," Teed said.

On August 1, Astoria Financial Corp issued a statement saying its shareholders approved the proposed merger of Greater New York Savings Bank into its Astoria Federal Savings and Loan Association unit.
